asleep.text: (Fast asleep. Best not to wake them.)
asleep.speaker: narrator

room.text: Shut the door, you're letting the weather in. You've the look of someone who walked a long way to stand in my doorway dripping.

choices.text: Is it always this wet here?

weather.text: Only in spring, summer and autumn. Winter's mostly ice. You'll want a room, then.

room2.text: First one up the stairs, on the left. Bed's dry, which puts it ahead of you. Where've you come from, then?

choices.text: From the coast, a long way west.
From the hill farms. I've worked a lot of harvests.
Here and there. I don't stay anywhere long.

room3.text: Well, you're here now. Here's the key. Breakfast is whatever Maren didn't sell yesterday, supper's stew. Keep to the roads after dark, Ilse gets twitchy about strangers in hedges.

choices.text: Is there work in the village?

work.text: Work finds people here, mostly by the notice board outside the Hall. And if Tobin Ashby comes in looking like a wet sheep, it's his pump again. You could do worse than help him.

main.text: Back again? The fire's going, at least.

choices.text: What's the news around the village?
How long have you kept the inn?

variants.text: Evening. Mind Garrick, he's had one cider and thinks he's a philosopher.
Rain again. Half the village is in here and the other half's thinking about it.

news.text: Bridge east is still out, so the carters are grumpy and the cider's selling. Sabine and Maren are at it over that empty stall. And Corin's been 'leaving tomorrow' for a week.

variants.text: Tobin's pump runs again, so he's stopped sighing into his soup. The bridge east is still out. And Corin is still leaving tomorrow.

hearth.text: Help yourself, just don't burn my soup pot. You'll cook better with a recipe than with hope.

history.text: Eleven years. My mother before me. I know every traveler by their boots and their bad habits.

history2.text: Wet boots. Asks a lot of questions. I'll reserve judgment on the bad habits.
